hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever had a question about faith you didn’t feel you could ask out loud?
options: then this one is for you. you’re in good company. listen.
thank you for saying so. hold onto it while you listen.
good. keep this one for a friend who might.

steps.line: The Qur’an tells how Ibrahim, Abraham, looked up one night and saw a bright star. “This is my Lord,” he said. Then the star set.

steps.q: The star is gone. What do you think Ibrahim says?
o: “I’ll wait for it to rise again.”
“Then the moon must be my Lord.”
steps.why: “I don’t love things that set.” Whatever disappears can’t be the answer.

steps.line: “I don’t love things that set,” he said. Then the moon rose, shining. “This is my Lord.” But the moon set too.
Then the sun came up, bigger than all of them. “This is greater.” And it set. So he turned to the One who made the heavens and the earth.

steps.q: Scholars read the star, the moon and the sun two ways. One: a young man searching. What’s the other?
o: A dream he had as a boy
A test the angels set for him
steps.why: Many scholars hold he was reasoning out loud for his star-worshiping people; others see a real search. Both readings end with the One who made them all.

steps.line: Later, the Qur’an says, he asked God: “Show me how You give life to the dead.” “Don’t you believe?” “Yes, but so that my heart may be at ease.”

steps.q: Ibrahim asks to see how God gives life to the dead. He’s told to take some birds. How many?
steps.why: Four (Qur’an 2:260), set on far hills and then called. Early commentators guessed which birds, a peacock and a rooster among them, though the Qur’an doesn’t say.

steps.line: He wasn’t scolded. He was shown: four birds, set on far hills, came flying back to him in haste when he called.
Centuries later, some companions told the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ they had thoughts too troubling to say aloud. “That,” he told them, “is clear faith.”
steps.label: a saying of the Prophet ﷺ

steps.q: Ibrahim asked God to show him. Muslims still give him a title of closeness. What is it?
o: Kalimullah, the one God spoke to
steps.why: Khalilullah, God’s close friend (Qur’an 4:125). Kalimullah is Musa’s title and Ruhullah is ‘Isa’s. The friend of God was also the one who asked.

say: here’s what i love. ibrahim asked, and he wasn’t sent away. he was shown.
many muslim scholars teach that iman, faith, can grow and dip and grow again. a question you bring to God, looking for rest, has been part of the path since ibrahim.

steps.q: The companions were ashamed of their thoughts. Why would the Prophet ﷺ call that “clear faith”?
o: He wanted them to stop dwelling on it
Their alarm showed faith was alive
steps.why: Not the thought itself. Scholars like an-Nawawi explain that their dread of it, and pushing it away, was the clear faith.

today.say: if there’s a question you’ve been carrying, write it down tonight, or bring it to an imam or someone you trust. and if a night question ever comes with real darkness, please reach out: 988 in the US, or local emergency help.
options: good. a question on paper is a question you can carry, like ibrahim did.
beautiful. the companions did exactly that.

card.keepWhy: Keep asking, so the heart can rest.
sources: Qur’an 6:75–79 (Ibrahim and the star, the moon and the sun: “I love not things that set”; “I have turned my face toward Him who created the heavens and the earth”), paraphrased
Qur’an 2:260 (“Show me how Thou givest life to the dead … Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease”; the four birds on the hills, coming in haste)
Sahih Muslim 132 (the companions’ troubling thoughts: “that is clear faith”)
check: Qur’an 6:75–79: commentators differ on whether Ibrahim was truly searching or arguing with his star-worshipping people step by step. The lesson tells it as the Qur’an does and doesn’t decide. Confirm, since this is the lesson’s main story on doubt.
Caption 1 says he looked up “one night” and the lesson moves from the stars (6:76) to the later request (2:260) with “later”. The Qur’an doesn’t give the order in time. Confirm “later”.
The birds (2:260): the verse says to take four birds, train them, place a part of them on each hill and call them. The lesson softens this to “four birds, set on far hills”. Confirm.
Teach line 2 says “many muslim scholars teach” that faith grows and dips (48:4); Hanafi/Maturidi scholars hold that faith itself doesn’t increase or decrease. Confirm the wording.
